title: Ingress Terraform module: blue/green TLS cert rotation and health-probe policies for internal NLB+ALB
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Implement a reusable Terraform module for internal VPC ingress that composes an NLB for TCP passthrough to an ALB for TLS termination and HTTP routing. The module must support automated certificate rotation (ACM/managed certs), a blue/green deployment pattern for ALB target groups, robust health probe configuration compatible with our control-plane and onprem components, and a safe rollout path for private clusters. Goals: 1) single module consumable by Private control plane and Edge Proxy stacks, 2) deterministic health check defaults and overrides per service, 3) automated cert lifecycle with zero-downtime rotation, and 4) clear Terraform upgrade path across major provider and module versions. This ticket covers design, TF module implementation, upgrade compatibility shims, docs, tests, and rollout playbook.
updates: 2026-02-26: Ticket created after spike comparing approaches: ALB-mostly vs NLB-passthrough + ALB TLS. Decided on NLB+ALB composition for private deployments to preserve source IPs and support internal TLS offload.

2026-03-02: Prototype module scaffolded (main.tf, variables.tf, outputs.tf). Added support for optional existing ACM cert ARN and automated request_flow for new certs. Initial unit tests with terraform-validate passing.
2026-03-05: Design review with Infra and Security. Security requested short cert TTL mitigation and audit log hooks. Added requirement for tagging and KMS key reference for any private cert stores.

2026-03-08: Implemented blue/green target group switching using weighted listener rules and a canary window variable. Added health-check template with HTTP/HTTPS/TCP modes and success_threshold/interval tuning.

2026-03-10: Opened PR #1123 against infra-modules repo. CI green for basic plan; found provider upgrade diff for aws provider v5 -> v6 causing listener rule argument changes. Added compatibility shim and transform in module to support both provider versions.
Next: address feedback from network team about cross-AZ subnet mapping, add e2e smoke tests using a temporary control-plane in a sandbox VPC, and draft runbook for manual rollback scenarios.
notes: Decision: Use NLB in front to preserve client source IPs for downstream internal services and metrics. ALB performs TLS termination and path-based routing to service target groups.
Trade-off: Adds one hop and additional cost (NLB + ALB) but simplifies certificate management and avoids ALB TCP limitations in cross-account VPC peering scenarios.
Compatibility: Implemented conditionals to emit legacy aws_lb_listener resources for provider v5 and aws_lb_listener_rule for v6+; documented known terraform-provider-aws diffs.
Security: Module surfaces KMS key id and audit log ARN variables; rotation events emit to CloudWatch Events (or EventBridge) for downstream monitoring.
Observed risk: simultaneous cert rotation and target-group switch could create transient 502s if health checks are too strict; plan to implement staggered rotation with health-check warmup window.
Alternative considered: AWS Gateway Load Balancer + ALB combo — rejected because gwlb complexity and limited internal routing features increased operational burden.
acceptance_criteria: Module passes terraform validate/plan/apply in sandbox account with both provider v5 and v6 without manual edits
Certificate rotation completes with zero 5xx error increase in synthetic traffic tests (pre/post comparison)
Blue/green rollout can shift 0->100% traffic within configurable canary window and be reverted without manual infra changes
Health checks detect unhealthy targets and ALB/NLB metrics surface meaningful alerts (unhealthy_count, latency, 4xx/5xx ratios)
Runbook and upgrade notes published in Confluence with explicit terraform state migration steps and rollback procedures
testing_plan: Unit: terraform validate and terraform fmt on module code, check conditional branches for provider compatibility
Integration: apply module into ephemeral sandbox VPC, create sample service behind ALB, validate HTTP and TLS routes
E2E: perform synthetic traffic storm during cert rotation and blue/green switch, assert no more than 0.5% error increase
Chaos: simulate AZ failure by failing targets and confirm healthy failover and alerting
Upgrade test: run terraform plan/apply after bumping provider locally to ensure shims work
runbook_summary: Pre-checks: verify terraform state backup, validate subnet mapping and cross-zone target registration
Cert rotation steps: create new cert, attach to ALB listener, wait for healthy checks, switch weights to new target group, deprecate old cert after 1 hour
Rollback: revert listener weights, reattach previous cert, apply module with force_replace=false to avoid recreations
Monitoring: dashboards to watch - ALB TargetResponseTime, UnHealthyHostCount, NLB FlowLogs errors, synthetic request success rate
Contacts: oncall-networking@redwood.ai, infra-owners team, security-eng for KMS issues
implementation_notes: Module exposes variables for existing NLB/ALB ARNs or will create new ones if omitted
Provide an opt-in managed_acm boolean; when true, module requests and validates ACM certs in the deployment region
Blue/green implemented via two target groups and listener rule weight; can be toggled to simple replacement for small services
Health check presets: control-plane (HTTP 443 /health z=3/interval=10s), onprem connectors (TCP probe / 10s), override allowed per consumer
Documented known issue: provider v6 changed default for listener.sni_policy; module maps both behaviors behind a var to avoid drift
